{"notes":"MOTIVATING SCENARIO, added 2026-09-15 as a forward-compatibility test of this epic.

A very-high-security 2028 deployment: paired IR cameras in the top two corners
of the display, looking down at the principal, running facial recognition, face
map, blood-vessel and liveness detection continuously, either in their own box
or as an OS process.

WHAT IT CONFIRMS THE DESIGN GETS RIGHT. It is an ordinary Attestor: enumerates
the enrolled operator, proves, reports freshness. It proves SILENTLY -- no
touch, no PIN -- so persona-jl4j.3's proof-cost field files it into the set
FetchJWTSVID may return unprompted. That validates keeping attainable tier and
proof cost as two INDEPENDENT fields: here the highest-assurance source
imaginable is also the cheapest to invoke, and a model assuming stronger implies
more expensive implies prompts would have mis-sorted it. hire_max_age is also
the right lever already -- a consumer asking for an observation no older than
two seconds is a request only a continuous sensor can satisfy. And pseudonymity
holds well: the face map never leaves the daemon, the consumer receives a
pseudonym plus a presence assertion, so biometrics get USED without being
DISTRIBUTED.

WHAT IT SHARPENS IN THIS EPIC.

persona-3tly.2 (presence and verification conflated) -- the sharpest possible
case. The cameras observe user presence and user verification separately and
continuously. A FIDO2 touch fuses them into one button press; this does not.

persona-3tly.5 (presence is not a scalar) -- PresenceLevel is a four-rung
ladder ending at Hardware (hire-core/src/assurance.rs:68-81). The cameras are
not rung five. A FIDO2 touch proves a finger pressed a button: not whose, and
not that they are still there one second later. The cameras prove which human,
continuously. A different KIND, not a greater HEIGHT. Resist adding a rung.

persona-3tly.6 (presence ends two ways) -- .6 is right and already names card
withdrawal, screen lock and session end. What it does not cover is a source
that emits no departure EVENT at all, because it emits a continuous truth and
departure is the ABSENCE of a fresh observation. Split out as persona-3tly.7.

persona-3tly.4 (record the limits in the spec) -- SPEC-HIRE currently does not
mention screen lock or card removal anywhere, so none of .6's analysis has
reached the document.

WHAT IT ADDED OUTSIDE THIS EPIC: persona-ux32, on calibrating trust in external
attestors. Note the framing correction recorded there -- hired already trusts
external authorities on every request, so the sensor-in-its-own-box is the
ssh-agent architecture at a higher tier, not a new category."}
